requirements.acceptance: EvidenceClaim raises for status met with an empty policy_quote and for status met with no non-blank citation. Non-met statuses need neither. check_claims reports each violating row separately instead of stopping at the first.
requirements.rationale: Structured output guarantees the shape of an evidence row, not that a met row carries support. An uncited met is not uncertainty a reviewer should weigh; it is an unsupported assertion, and routing it to a human relaxes the rule into a suggestion.
requirements.statement: A criterion marked met carries both a non-empty policy quote and at least one chart-side citation. A met claim missing either is rejected before any determination is drafted.

requirements.acceptance: resolve_citations keeps citations that resolve, strips malformed or unresolvable ones with a "CITATION STRIPPED" note in the summary, keeps the criterion met only if at least one citation survives, downgrades it to insufficient otherwise, and leaves non-met claims untouched.
requirements.rationale: A prompt cannot guarantee that a cited reference is real. Resolving each citation against the bundle is a deterministic check, so a fabricated reference cannot support a claim however confident the model sounds.
requirements.statement: A citation that does not resolve against the submitted bundle is stripped and logged, and a met criterion with no surviving citation is downgraded to insufficient.

requirements.acceptance: The decision enum in the drafter's response schema is exactly {approve, insufficient_evidence}, and the Determination type admits the same two values.
requirements.rationale: A drafted denial anchors the reviewer toward denying, which hollows out human review even when the routing is technically correct.
requirements.statement: The determination drafter can emit only approve or insufficient_evidence. The AI never drafts a denial; a human forms and owns any denial.

requirements.acceptance: verify_chain accepts an untouched log and raises ChainBrokenError after an entry's content is edited, after an entry is deleted, and after entries are reordered.
requirements.rationale: An audit trail that can be edited without trace is a narrative, not a record. The chain makes casual tampering evident; it does not resist a party who can rewrite the whole file, and this claim does not say it does.
requirements.statement: Decision logs are hash-chained: editing, deleting or reordering an entry is detected on verification.

requirements.acceptance: confidence_gate routes an approve at or above the threshold with no gaps to auto; routes an approve below the threshold to review; routes insufficient_evidence to review at any confidence; routes an approve with a required criterion insufficient to review at any confidence; and does not force review for a non-required insufficient criterion alone.
requirements.behavioural_statement: Approvals at or above the configured confidence threshold with no required criterion insufficient are routed to automatic finalization; every other case is routed to review. Whether 0.85 is the right boundary is not supported by evidence about this system.
requirements.rationale: Automatic finalization is the point at which the system acts and nobody will overrule it. The rule that lets a draft through is therefore a decision boundary, and a boundary needs evidence, not a round number.
requirements.statement: Only an approval is finalized automatically, and only when its confidence reaches the threshold and no required criterion is insufficient. Every other case goes to a human.

requirements.acceptance: Determination accuracy on a labelled set, with a stated interval.
requirements.rationale: Named so that a bundle which says nothing about determination accuracy is not read as having covered it.
requirements.scope_note: Measured in prior-auth-agent's own golden evaluation (its EVALS.md), on recorded model output. It is not asserted or re-measured in this run.
requirements.statement: The drafted determination agrees with clinical ground truth.

requirements.acceptance: Recall of the labelled passage at the retrieval depth the pipeline uses.
requirements.rationale: If retrieval returns the wrong policy, later reasoning can be sound and the answer still wrong. That failure is invisible to the claims above.
requirements.scope_note: Requires the vector store and the policy corpus. Retrieval quality is not evaluated at the pinned revision.
requirements.statement: Retrieval surfaces the policy passage that each criterion is drawn from.

requirements.rationale: An infrastructure property, not a property of the code exercised here.
requirements.scope_note: The repository's Terraform is documentation-grade and has never been applied, so there is no deployment to verify against.
requirements.statement: Patient data stays inside the deployment's PHI boundary.

requirements.acceptance: Binding.is_trusted is True for VERIFIED and False for every other status, including DEPRECATED.
requirements.rationale: A provisional binding is a developer's assertion that two codes mean the same thing. Downstream, a CodeableConcept carries no visible difference between an asserted mapping and one checked against an authoritative release, so the distinction has to be enforced at the boundary or it is lost permanently.
requirements.statement: A terminology binding is reported as trusted only when its status is VERIFIED. There is no implicit promotion from PROVISIONAL.

requirements.acceptance: procedure_binding, observation_binding, ucum_unit and procedure_status each raise UnmappedConceptError on an unknown input, and the error names the offending code and its domain.
requirements.rationale: An uncoded CodeableConcept is worse than a missing one: it looks like valid data and is invisible to every query that matters. Refusing is the only behaviour that surfaces the gap while it is still cheap to fix.
requirements.statement: A local code with no binding raises UnmappedConceptError. The pipeline never emits an uncoded concept in place of a coded one.

requirements.acceptance: verified + provisional == total == len(all_bindings()), and each count matches an independent recount of the table by status.
requirements.rationale: The report is the only place the provisional fraction becomes visible to anyone who is not reading the source. A governance metric that can drift from the thing it measures is worse than no metric.
requirements.statement: coverage_report() reports the trusted fraction of the concept map, and its counts reconcile with the binding table it summarises.

requirements.acceptance: administrative_gender(None) and administrative_gender("wat") both return "unknown"; no exception is raised.
requirements.behavioural_statement: Unknown and absent gender values return "unknown".
requirements.rationale: Administrative gender is not clinically load-bearing in this pipeline and FHIR defines "unknown" as a valid value, so refusing the case would drop a whole surgical record over a field nothing depends on. The exception is defensible; leaving it undeclared is not, because the next reader cannot tell it from an oversight.
requirements.statement: administrative_gender degrades an unknown value to "unknown" rather than raising, as a deliberate and bounded exception to the fail-loud rule.

requirements.acceptance: The provisional fraction is at or below a defined ceiling.
requirements.behavioural_statement: The verified/provisional split is measured and published. Whether it is adequate is not decided anywhere in the system.
requirements.rationale: Stated deliberately as the claim someone would make in a sales conversation or an integration review, to show what the harness does with it. The pipeline measures the split honestly and publishes it; nothing consumes the number to gate anything, so there is no boundary behind the word "fit".
requirements.statement: The concept map is fit for clinical exchange.

requirements.acceptance: map_case returns no resources and an ERROR-severity issue naming the element.
requirements.rationale: The pipeline's central design decision. Verified upstream by test_unmapped_procedure_code_drops_case.
requirements.scope_note: Requires mapping.py and the synthetic case generator. This run scopes to the terminology-trust layer.
requirements.statement: A case with an unmapped procedure code or missing laterality is dropped rather than degraded.

requirements.acceptance: No source identifier value appears in any emitted resource.
requirements.rationale: The pipeline's identifier boundary, enforced upstream by test_no_raw_mrn_leaks_into_output.
requirements.scope_note: Requires mapping.py. Named here because an evidence bundle that silently omits the identifier-boundary claim invites the reader to assume it was covered.
requirements.statement: No raw medical record number reaches FHIR output.

requirements.acceptance: exchangeable_rate reconciles with cases_in and cases_dropped, and error_by_element accounts for every drop.
requirements.rationale: The pipeline's headline deliverable. Verified upstream.
requirements.statement: The quality report states the exchangeable fraction and attributes every dropped case to the element that caused the drop.
